answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring a steady pulse of verifiable completed work before any identity earns high-value access. Newcomers start with tiny limits and must accumulate audited history over time; a sudden plume of brand-new identities all chasing the same reward is easy to spot and throttle, while an umber flag in the registry marks accounts whose work history does not match their claims until a human or auditor clears them.
